newsitem.title: USA: HCIA stock suffers second big collapse.
newsitem.headline: HCIA stock suffers second big collapse.

text.p: The stock of HCIA Inc suffered its second major selloff in nine months on Monday, losing over half its value after the company said it expected second-quarter results well below Wall Street expectations.

HCIA said it was expecting a loss for the quarter ended June 30 of between $0.15 and $0.18 a share due to a revenue shortfall in two of its units. Analysts had expected earnings of $0.30 for the second quarter, according to First Call.
The stock was off 16-15/16 to 15-1/16 in early afternoon trading and was one of the most active issues on the Nasdaq market.
The Baltimore-based company develops and supplies clinical and financial information systems for the health care industry.
It suffered a similar collapse on October 1, falling by almost half to 32-28/32 from 60 after warning weak revenues would drag its third quarter 1996 earnings well below analysts' expectations.

HCIA said Monday its latest disappointment was largely due to second quarter revenue shortfalls in its provider solutions unit. And it said the unit's earnings in the third and fourth quarter were also likely to fall short of expectations.
The unit, which provides cost and efficiency benchmark tools to hundreds of hospitals, was formed after the August 1996 acquisition of LBA Health Care Management Inc.
HCIA said its second-quarter results would also be hurt by failure of its commercial markets and managed care units to secure several significant agreements during the quarter.

Steven Halper, an analyst for Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette, said HCIA failed to secure two large contracts expected in its supplier area that serves larger customers in the pharmaceutical, medical device and supply markets.
"The contracts would have covered shortfalls they had in their (hospital) provider area," he said.
Halper said HCIA, which went public in 1994, would continue to be dependent quarter by quarter on such large software deals.
"They're a small company. Every quarter will be challenging for them until they become a big company," he said. "It's a high-risk, high reward scenario."
Halper said he was continuing his market performer rating on HCIA. Alex. Brown downgraded HCIA to market perform from strong buy Monday morning.
